8. Arguments heard.

9. It has been argued by Ld. Addl. PP for State that marriage between the accused Sonu and deceased lasted only for a period of around one and half years suggesting that everything was not well within the family.
It has been submitted that direct evidence was hardly available in such cases when the incident had occurred within the four walls of a house.

It has been submitted that there is ample evidence on record to suggest that soon before her death, deceased was subjected to cruelty pertaining to demand of dowry so presumption u/s 113B of Indian Evidence Act was required to be applied in these facts.
It has been submitted that as per PW2, he had talked with the deceased on 09.08.2020 over phone wherein she had told him about being harassed by accused persons.
It has been submitted that similarly PW3 also stated about the accused having given beatings to his sister and about the call dated 09.08.2020.
It has been submitted that the fact that accused Sonu had shown another lady in Safdarjung hospital to PW3 as the deceased in itself raises suspicion.

It has been submitted that admittedly death of deceased was unnatural as she had consumed poison that too of such a nature which was not readily available and which cannot be digested by anyone through food and water accidentally.
It has been submitted that statements of PW2 and 3 recorded by SDM corroborates the case of prosecution.

It has been submitted that though a defence is being taken to the effect that deceased was suffering from depression, however, it has come on record during the cross-examination of accused Sonu that deceased was not suffering from any illness nor she was taking any medicine.

It has been submitted that had she been suffering from depression,
she would have been taking medicine for the same.

It has been submitted that family of accused as well as that of deceased were of poor financial background and no dowry whatsoever was given during marriage of accused Sonu Kumar with deceased.

11. In rebuttal, it has been submitted by Ld. Counsel for complainant while assisting Ld. Addl. PP for State that no bottle/container of poison was found by police at the spot.

It has been submitted that CDR pertaining to mobile number belonging to accused Ram Chander on record shows that calls were made between the deceased and PW-2 on 09.08.2020 thereby strengthening the case of prosecution.

It has been submitted that it has come on record in the testimony of PW-3 that he had seen the swollen face of his sister when accused Sonu and Ritu had come to drop her off at Shakurpur Metro Station.
12. I have considered the submissions from both the sides alongwith record.
13. Record shows that accused persons have been charged with for commission of offences U/s 498A/304B/34 IPC and Section 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.

13.1 Sections 498-A provides as under- "498-A. Husband or relative of husband of a woman subjecting her to cruelty.--Whoever, being the husband or the relative of the husband of a woman,
subjects such woman to cruelty shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine.
Explanation.--For the purposes of this section

, "cruelty"
means-- (a) any wilful conduct which is of such a nature as is likely to drive the woman to commit suicide or to cause grave injury or danger to life, limb or health (whether mental or physical) of the woman; or (b) harassment of the woman where such harassment is with a view to coercing her or any person related to her to meet any unlawful demand for any property or valuable security or is on account of failure by her or any person related to her to meet such demand."
13.2 Section 304 B IPC provides as under- State vs Sonu Kumar on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12808679/
8 "304-B. Dowry death.--(1) Where the death of a woman is caused by any burns or bodily injury or occurs otherwise than under normal circumstances within seven years of her marriage and it is shown that soon before her death she was subjected to cruelty or harassment by her husband or any relative of her husband for, or in connection with, any demand for dowry, such death shall be called "dowry death",
and such husband or relative shall be deemed to have caused her death.
Explanation.--For the purpose of this sub-section, "dowry" shall have the same meaning as in Section 2 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 (28 of 1961).
( 2) Whoever commits dowry death shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than seven years but which may extend to imprisonment for life."

15. Section 113-B of the Indian Evidence Act provides as under:
"113-B. Presumption as to dowry death.-When the question is whether a person has committed the dowry death of a woman and it is shown that soon before her death such woman had been subjected by such person to cruelty or harassment for, or in connection with, any demand for dowry, the Court shall presume that such person had caused the dowry death.
Explanation.-For the purposes of this section, "dowry death" shall have the same meaning as in Section 304-B of Indian Penal Code (45 of 1860)."

16. As to when the presumption u/s 113 B shall apply in a given case, it was held by Hon'ble Apex Court in Karan Singh (Supra) as under- "The presumption under Section 113-B will apply when it is established that soon before her death, the woman has been subjected by the accused to cruelty or harassment for, or in connection with, any demand for dowry.

Therefore, even for attracting Section 113-B, the prosecution must establish that the deceased was State vs Sonu Kumar on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12808679/
9 subjected by the appellant to cruelty or harassment for or in connection with any demand of dowry soon before her death.
Unless these facts are proved, the presumptions under Section 113-B of the Evidence Act cannot be invoked."
17. Now the evidence on record shall be analyzed to see as to whether the prosecution has proved its case against the accused or not.
18. PW-2 Sh. Janak Manjhi (father of deceased) and Dinesh Kumar (brother of deceased) are the two material witnesses examined by prosecution to prove its case.

Before going through their testimonies, it is to be noted that there is no dispute to the fact that the marriage of deceased Ms.
Sheela @ Dharamsheela had been solemnized with accused Sonu Kumar on 29.05.2019.
This fact has been so admitted by accused Sonu Kumar in his testimony as DW-1.
Similarly there is no dispute to the fact that Ms. Sheela @ Dharamsheela had got expired on 10.08.2020.

Her MLC No.
195109 (Ex.PW-13/J) proves this fact as per which she was declared brought dead at 10:10AM in the hospital after her admission there at 09:15AM.
There is also no dispute to the fact that she had not died due to natural cause rather she had died due to poisoning.
The postmortem report Ex.PW-13/F mentions the cause of death as pending till receipt of viscera and Histopathological report.

As per FSL report regarding examination of Viscera (Ex.PA-4), the stomach and pieces of small intestine along with pieces of liver, spleen and kidney as well as blood sample of the deceased were found containing Organophosphorous Pesticide (Dichlorvos).
Histopathological Examination report Ex.PA-5 pertaining to the deceased shows some areas of necrotic patches in her pancreas on gross-examination.
On microscopic examination of pancreas, normal pancreatic tissue with focal area of necrosis and fatty degeneration was found.

On receiving both these reports, Investigating Officer Insp. Harender Singh (PW-10) had requested for subsequent opinion regarding cause of death vide his letter Ex.PW-10/B on which subsequent opinion Ex.PW-10/A was given as per which the cause of death was Organophosphorus Pesticide (Dichlorvos) poisoning.
So, it stands established that the death of Ms. Sheela @ Dharamsheela had not happened due to natural cause.

19. Though, at the fag end of trial during the course of final arguments, Ld. Counsel for complainant sought to make out a case of deliberate poisoning of deceased by accused Sonu Kumar and his family members however, it appears that case of prosecution throughout remains that the deceased had herself consumed poison to end her life.
So, the only question to be examined is at to whether the act of deceased in consuming poison was result of cruelty meted to her in connection with demand of dowry.
Testimonies of PW-2 Sh. Janak Manjhi and PW-3 Sh. Dinesh Kumar are material for proving this particular aspect.

20. In his testimony, PW-2 Sh. Janak Manjhi stated that his daughter Dharamsheela had got married with accused Sonu on 29.05.2019 according to Hindu rites and ceremonies and that she had started staying with him along with his family members in the area of Chhattarpur in Delhi.
He stated that before marriage, accused Sonu had demanded a motorcycle, gold ring and gold chain and that accused persons had delayed the ceremony of tilak and had started creating trouble.
He stated that thereafter, he yielded to their demand and gave a second hand motorcycle which was being used by his son along with one gold ring and had promised to give gold chain after marriage.

He stated that when accused Sonu alongwith his wife came to Delhi, all four accused persons used to State vs Sonu Kumar on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12808679/
10 harass his daughter and used to throw tantrums as they have been given a second hand motorcycle.
They also used to demand gold chain from his daughter and used to harass her.
He stated that accused persons quarrelled with his daughter and used to beat her and hurl abuses against her.
He stated that he came to know these things on being informed by her on call and that he had made her understand to adjust with them.
He stated that he had also called Sonu but he told him that he was not having time and asked him to call his family members.
He stated that on 9th August, one day before the death of Ms. Dharamsheela, his daughter had called him and told that she was not knowing as to what will happen.
She also told him that Sonu used to beat her due to which she used to get unconscious.
She further told him that Nageshwari, Ramchander and Ritu Devi used to harass her.
He stated that he told his daughter that he will inform her brother Dinesh who was residing in Chhattarpur, Delhi and that he will visit her house to see the condition.

He stated that on 10 th August, Ram Chander (father-in-law of deceased) called him and asked as to whether his daughter was having a problem of mirgi to which he replied that she was staying with them for so long and that they must be aware of symptoms of mirgi.
He stated that he was then informed that his daughter had expired.
He further stated that Ram Chander had also called his son Chandan who informed him that Ram Chander had asked same question from him.
He stated that thereafter, he called accused Sonu and asked as to what had happened to Dharamsheela to which he was informed that she was perfectly fine and was being taken to hospital for treatment.
He stated that he asked his son Dinesh to visit hospital to see Dharmasheela where accused Sonu used to work as compounder.
He stated that when he reached there, he was shown another lady saying that his sister was getting treatment.
When he went nearby the patient he found that she was not his sister.
He stated that his daughter was harassed for dowry by accused Sonu and killed her by administering poison.

He stated that the dead body was received by his son from the hospital and that he was called by police officials on which he came to Delhi on 13 th August in a bus with great difficulty as he could not get train ticket due to Corona period.

He stated that after reaching Delhi, he went to hospital where he identified the dead body of his daughter vide identification memo Ex.PW-2/A and that his statement was recorded by SDM as Ex.PW-2/B.

BR04N3822 executed by one Jawahar Yadav in favour of his son Chandan Manjhi Mark PW-2/D2 (OSR) (running into 2 pages) and submitted that original thereof was given to accused Sonu alongwith motorcycle at the time of marriage.
He denied the suggestion that documents placed on record by him on that day were fabricated.

He denied the suggestion that on 02.07.2020, accused Sonu had called him and requested him to talk to Dharamsheela as she was not well and that he had refuesd to do so by saying ki marti hai to mar jaye.

In his cross-examination by Ld. Defence Counsel, he stated that the marriage of his sister was solemnized at the native village i.e., Matiyar, District Chhapra and that they had given sewing machine, refrigerator, bed and utensils by way of dowry to the accused persons at the time of tilak.

He stated that he was working as a cutting master of clothes in a factory in Wazirpur Industrial Area and that he used to earn around Rs. 30,000/- per month at that time after including payment for overtime.
He stated that a part of salary used to be credited in his bank account and remaining part used to be paid in cash because that would have meant higher contribution deduction on the part of employer.

He stated that the demand of motorcycle was made on the day State vs Sonu Kumar on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12808679/
13 of tilak.

He stated that he visited his sister at her matrimonial home around 4-5 time however, he was unable to recollect the exact date of his visit to her matrimonial home when he had tried to make the accused persons understand not to torture her.

He admitted that his sister was never beaten by accused persons in his presence and that he along with his family members i.e., his sister Usha, brother Chandan and his wife had visited Chhatarpur Temple however, he was unable to say as to whether the date of said visit was 05.11.2019.
He admitted that his sister Dharamsheela along with accused Sonu and Ritu had also come there at that time.
He denied the suggestion that on that day Dharamsheela had requested him to take her with him however, he had refused to do so.
He admitted that accused Sonu had brought Dharamsheela to his home afterwards.
He volunteered to say that they had come there after having a fight.
He denied the suggestion that during the stay of Dharamsheela with him for around one month, he used to pressurize her to return to her matrimonial home or that he told her that he will not keep her.
He also denied the suggestion that he had never visited his sister Dharamsheela at her matrimonial home after November 2019.
He denied the suggestion that Dharamsheela wanted to visit his new born son however, he refused to allow her to do so or that his sister was under depression as they had stopped meeting her.
His attention was drawn to the documents Ex.PW-2/D1 on record and he was put suggestion to the effect that documents were false and fabricated which was denied by him.
He admitted that the motorcycle given by them was currently with Timal and volunteered to say that only accused Sonu can tell as to how same was with him.
He stated that he talked with his sister for the last time on 03.08.2020.
He was unable to say as to whether his father had told his sister Dharamsheela not to visit him in the village 2-3 days before her death.
He denied the suggestion that it was a simple marriage or that accused persons had never demanded any dowry.
He also denied the suggestion that his sister was given all possible basic necessities of life.
24. Perusal of aforementioned testimony of PW-2 shows that allegations leveled by him are vague and general in nature.
PW-2 stated that all four accused persons used to harass his daughter on the issue of Motorcycle and Gold Chain.
He also stated that they used to quarrel with her and beat her on these issues.
Regarding his source of information, he stated that he was informed by his daughter on call.
He did not specify as to on which date, month or year, he had received those calls.
Prosecution has not placed on record CDR pertaining to his mobile number which could have shown as to whether he was regularly in touch with his daughter.
It is also not clear as to what steps were taken by him on being informed by his daughter of ill treatment being meted out to her.
As admitted by witness in his cross-examination, he never came to Delhi to see his daughter.
It is surprising that he did not make any attempt to see her even after having knowledge of accused persons treating her with cruelty.

In case, he was unable to come to Delhi to see her for any reason including old age/poverty etc, he could have easily asked his son Dinesh who was residing with his family in Delhi to go and check on her and to do the needful including taking necessary legal action.
This conduct of PW-2 raises serious doubt on the veracity of allegations leveled by him against the accused persons.

25. Moving further, much emphasis has been laid by Prosecution as well as Complainant on the part of testimony of PW-2 wherein he stated that he had received a call from the deceased on 09 th August 2020, wherein she had reiterated her allegations against the accused persons including that Sonu used to beat her so badly that she used to get unconscious.
It has been argued that same was enough to show that she was treated with cruelty soon before her death.

14 9971726319 belonging to accused Ram Chander (which was being used by accused Sonu for last 15 years as per his cross-examination) for the period 10.07.2020 to 10.08.2020 (Ex. PA-7) on record shows that a call was made from that number to the mobile number 7765855230 on 09.08.2020 for 208 seconds at 11:07:36 hrs.

ASJ-02, South on 11.08.2021 during hearing of anticipatory bail application of accused), he stated that he had talked with his daughter and son-in-law on 09.08.2020 and everything was fine on that day.

Defence Counsel to follow the procedure prescribed under Section 162 Cr.P.C. read with Section 145 Indian Evidence Act (as authoritatively held by Hon'ble Apex Court in Constitution Bench judgment titled as Tahsildar Singh And Anr. Vs. The State of Uttar Pradesh AIR1959SC1012), apparent contradictions in the testimony of PW-2 from his previous statements can not be considered by this Court.

sentences.text: Still, the fact remains that if the witness had talked to his daughter on 09.08.2020 in the morning when she had told him about the harassment / beatings being given by accused persons, it is not clear as to why he did not take any immediate steps including to inform his son Dinesh to either visit his Sister or to call police to lodge a complaint in this regard.
His failure to do so makes his testimony untrustworthy.

26. Perusal of testimony of PW-3 Dinesh Kumar Manjhi shows that as per him, the information regarding his sister being harassed/beaten up for demand of dowry by accused persons was conveyed by her to their father on phone.
It appears that the facts deposed by him in this regard are based on hearsay.
Apart form that, he has stated about his sister having being brought to Shakurpur Metro Station 5 months prior to her death and at that time, he had observed that her face was swollen.
He stated that his sister had told him that she was beaten up by all the accused persons and that he had requested accused Sonu and Ritu to accompany them to his home but they refused.
In his testimony as DW-1 (in his cross-examination), accused Sonu admitted that he along with his sister Ritu had taken the deceased Dharamsheela to Shakurpur Metro Station.
He volunteered to say that they had called Dinesh Manjhi there as they were not knowing the location of his house.
He admitted that Dinesh had requested them to accompany him to his house but they refused to do so.
He volunteered to say that it was late in the night.
So, in view of the Court, nothing much should be read in their refusal to go to the house of PW-3.
PW-3 further stated that accused Ritu and Sonu were saying that they will not keep his sister in their house and that Sonu will be re-married which was denied by DW-1 in his cross- examination.

As per PW-3, he had complained about the conduct of accused persons to his Mausa, Mausi and their sons Timal (with whom, another sister of Sonu had been married and the marriage of deceased with Sonu was solemnized through them) but none of them was examined as a witness by prosecution to prove this thing.

PW-3 further stated in his testimony that on 03.08.2020, while his wife was admitted in hospital, he had called his sister and found that she was crying over the call saying that all the four accused persons had given beatings to State vs Sonu Kumar on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12808679/
15 her.
He stated that he told her that he will come to her matrimonial house to bring her back to his house.
No CDR pertaining to mobile number of PW-3 is on record to show that any such call was exchanged between them.

Also, in case his sister had complained about being beaten up by the accused persons and he had promised her to bring her to his house, it is not clear as to why he did not do any such thing till next one week.
In any case, he could have easily made call to police at 100 number to complain about the conduct of accused persons but admittedly no such call was ever made.

Prosecution has placed much reliance on the portion of testimony of PW-3 wherein he stated that accused Sonu had given him wrong information about his sister being well and glucose being administered to her.

He also stated about his visit to Safdarjung Hospital whereupon Sonu had shown him another lady as his sister to whom glucose was being administered but when he carefully watched that lady, he found that she was not his sister.
Later on, he along with her elder brother found dead body of their sister on a separate bed in the emergency ward.
In view of the Court, even if this version of PW-3 is accepted as correct still same is of no help to the case of prosecution.
May be, the correct information was not given immediately under fear as the deceased was sister of PW-3 or may be, the accused was not willing to break the bad bad news at the first instance.

In any case,
this particular conduct of accused Sonu was not enough to prove the ingredients of offences against him and his family members.

At the cost of repetition, it is required to be noted that despite PW-2 and PW-3 allegedly having information regarding harassment of deceased including repeated beatings being given to her by the accused persons for bringing dowry in the form of new motorcycle and gold chain, they did not take any step against them.
No complaint was made to police or any other authority.
PW-2 even never visited the house of deceased.
PW-3 stated that he had visited her house once or twice but he was unable to tell the date of such visits.

In these circumstances, the defence of accused reiterated by accused Sonu in his testimony as DW-1 that deceased used to remain tense and used to cry as no one from her family ever visited her at her matrimonial home and that she was not even allowed to see new born son of her brother Dinesh can not be brushed aside lightly.

27. It is also to be noted that one Ms. Gurdeep Kaur was examined as PW-1 in the present case wherein she has stated that accused Ram Chander Manjhi along with his wife Nageshwari Devi,
their son Sonu and their daughters Ritu and Barkha used to reside in her neighborhood since last around 15-20 years.
She also stated that after the marriage of Sonu with Sheela, they also used to reside with them at the said address.
She stated about the death of Sheela on 10.08.2020 and that she was not knowing the reason thereof.
In her cross-examination, she admitted that she used to visit the house of accused Ram Chander and that she had never noticed any quarrel between Sheela and Ram Chander or Nageshwari Devi.
She stated that they used to treat her as their daughter and that there was no demand of dowry by accused from Sheela.
She admitted that Sonu had never beaten Sheela in her presence and that she had never seen brother of Sheela namely Dinesh or her father ever visiting her.
So, an independent witness residing in the neighborhood of the accused has also deposed in their favor.

28. As far as allegations u/s 4, The Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 are concerned, as per PW-2, accused Sonu had demanded motorcycle, gold ring and gold chain before marriage and that accused persons had delayed the ceremony of Tilak on the ground that they had not been given motorcycle, gold ring and gold chain whereupon a second hand motorcycle being used by his son along with one gold ring State vs Sonu Kumar on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12808679/
16 was handed over to them and it was promised to give the gold chain later on.

PW-3 on the other hand stated that in the marriage ceremony, accused Sonu along with his father, mother and sister Ritu had demanded one new motorcycle and one gold chain but they had given a second hand motorcycle on their demand.
He neither stated anything about the demand of gold ring nor about any such gold ring having being given to the accused.
There is also contradiction on the point that who had made the demand for these dowry articles.
Moving further, as far as the issue of handing over of motorcycle number BRO4N3822 to the accused Sonu is concerned, it appears that the motorcycle was now with Timal.
Both PW-2 & PW-3 admitted that the motorcycle was now Timal Manjhi.
Their version is that they had given the motorcycle to Sonu and he had handed it over to Timal Manjhi later on.
As mentioned earlier, Timal Manjhi has not been examined as a witness in this case.
No such motorcycle was seized by police during investigation.
PW-2 placed on record certain documents PW-2/D1 (OSR) (colly, 8 pages) pertaining to the dowry articles given to accused at the time of marriage
however it is settled law that merely placing a document on record does not amount to its proof and that same is required to be proved as per law.
Admittedly, none of the shopkeepers who had issued those documents/invoices was examined by prosecution to prove the same.
The demand of dowry by accused persons from the deceased after marriage is also doubtful in view of discussion done earlier.
29. It is settled law that an accused is deemed innocent until proven guilty.
Prosecution is expected to prove its case against the accused beyond reasonable doubt.

Considering the above discussion,
this Court is of the view that prosecution has miserably failed to prove demand of dowry on the part of accused persons or cruetly pertaining thereto soon before death of Sheela@Dharamsheela.
Accused persons namely Sonu Kumar, Nageshwari Devi, Ram Chander and Ritu are accordingly acquitted.

It has been submitted that there is ample evidence on record to suggest that soon before her death, deceased was subjected to cruelty pertaining to demand of dowry so presumption u/s 113B of Indian Evidence Act was required to be applied in these facts.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
14. As held by Hon'ble Apex Court in Karan Singh Vs. State of Haryana, Crl Appeal No. 1076/2014,
following are the essential ingredients of Section 304-B IPC:
a) The death of a woman must have been caused by any burns or bodily injury, or must have occurred otherwise than under normal circumstances;
b) The death must have been caused within seven years of her marriage;
c) Soon before her death, she must have been subjected to cruelty or harassment by the husband or any relative of her husband; and d) Cruelty or harassment must be for, or in connection with, any demand for dowry.
15. Section 113-B of the Indian Evidence Act provides as under:
"113-B. Presumption as to dowry death.-When the question is whether a person has committed the dowry death of a woman and it is shown that soon before her death such woman had been subjected by such person to cruelty or harassment for, or in connection with, any demand for dowry, the Court shall presume that such person had caused the dowry death.
So, it stands established that the death of Ms. Sheela @ Dharamsheela had not happened due to natural cause.
Prosecution has not placed on record CDR pertaining to his mobile number which could have shown as to whether he was regularly in touch with his daughter.
It is also not clear as to what steps were taken by him on being informed by his daughter of ill treatment being meted out to her.
As admitted by witness in his cross-examination, he never came to Delhi to see his daughter.

This conduct of PW-2 raises serious doubt on the veracity of allegations leveled by him against the accused persons.
In his statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C. dated 14.08.2020 (seen and signed as such by the then Ld. ASJ-02, South on 11.08.2021 during hearing of anticipatory bail application of accused), he stated that he had talked with his daughter and son-in-law on 09.08.2020 and everything was fine on that day.
His attention was also not drawn to his earlier statements i.e., statement given to SDM Ex.PW-2/B and statement under Section 161 of Cr.P.C.
Due to failure of Ld. Defence Counsel to follow the procedure prescribed under Section 162 Cr.P.C. read with Section 145 Indian Evidence Act (as authoritatively held by Hon'ble Apex Court in Constitution Bench judgment titled as Tahsildar Singh And Anr. Vs. The State of Uttar Pradesh AIR1959SC1012), apparent contradictions in the testimony of PW-2 from his previous statements can not be considered by this Court.
May be, the correct information was not given immediately under fear as the deceased was sister of PW-3 or may be, the accused was not willing to break the bad bad news at the first instance.
In any case,
this particular conduct of accused Sonu was not enough to prove the ingredients of offences against him and his family members.
At the cost of repetition, it is required to be noted that despite PW-2 and PW-3 allegedly having information regarding harassment of deceased including repeated beatings being given to her by the accused persons for bringing dowry in the form of new motorcycle and gold chain, they did not take any step against them.

In these circumstances, the defence of accused reiterated by accused Sonu in his testimony as DW-1 that deceased used to remain tense and used to cry as no one from her family ever visited her at her matrimonial home and that she was not even allowed to see new born son of her brother Dinesh can not be brushed aside lightly.
28. As far as allegations u/s 4, The Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 are concerned, as per PW-2, accused Sonu had demanded motorcycle, gold ring and gold chain before marriage and that accused persons had delayed the ceremony of Tilak on the ground that they had not been given motorcycle, gold ring and gold chain whereupon a second hand motorcycle being used by his son along with one gold ring State vs Sonu Kumar on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12808679/
